correctness.rationale: First-attempt renewal of the Brownian fixed-target Laplace transform gives a closed analytic expression. Two derivatives yield exact positive conditional moments. Exponential-distance integration establishes precise first- and second-moment domains and formulas via Tonelli. The scaled analytic-transform convergence on a uniform disk gives conditional mth moments asymptotic to m! exp(m sqrt(r/D) R)/r^m and hence the all-integer-moment threshold including equality. Quadratic maximization proves both unique rate minima and 4/3 mean-cost tradeoff. Independent high-precision transform differentiation, numerical integration and higher-order scaled-moment checks passed; finite checks do not replace the analytic divergence proof.

value.rationale: The exponential target family is natural enough to be the exact conjugate family in the initiating mean-optimal-protocol work. Within this physically motivated family, optimization of mean search time gives an infinite passage-time variance, while reducing reset frequency by exactly a factor four yields the optimal finite CV sqrt(7) for only 4/3 the minimal mean. The complete integer moment spectrum is a structural, nontrivial phase classification of quenched search-time reliability rather than routine enumeration or a minor numerical gain.
